root_cause: The GOV.UK Tabs component interprets ArrowDown as a navigation key for a vertical tablist because the aria-orientation attribute is missing, causing focus to shift to the next tab when the down arrow is pressed.
repair_strategy: Add aria-orientation="horizontal" to the tablist (<ul>) element to explicitly declare the tablist's horizontal orientation, ensuring that only left/right arrow keys change the selected tab while up/down arrows have no effect on tab selection.

expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing the ArrowDown key while focus is on a tab will no longer change the selected tab; focus will remain on the same tab, preserving horizontal tab navigation behavior as required by WCAG 2.1.1 and 2.4.3.
functional_risks: Screen‑reader users who mistakenly expect vertical arrow navigation may experience a slight change in interaction pattern, but the visual presentation is horizontal so the risk is low.
Any custom script that relies on the absence of aria-orientation could behave differently; however, no such script is present in the supplied source.
verification_requirements: Verify that after pressing ArrowDown the aria-selected attribute remains on the originally focused tab.
Verify that ArrowLeft and ArrowRight still correctly change the selected tab and associated panel visibility.
Confirm that the tablist element in the DOM now includes aria-orientation="horizontal".
Ensure that pressing ArrowDown does not move focus to another element outside the tab.
Validate that the tab panels continue to show/hide correctly when tabs are changed via left/right arrows.
